html:
Sudan is a large country in northeast Africa on the middle Nile, with Khartoum as its capital. On the map it covers the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan and the republic that followed in 1956.

The Nile valley here was home to Kush and later Christian Nubian kingdoms. Egypt conquered the country in the 1820s. In 1881 Muhammad Ahmad, who called himself the Mahdi, led a revolt and founded an Islamic state. A British and Egyptian army destroyed it at Omdurman in 1898. Britain then ran the country in name jointly with Egypt.

  • 1925: the Gezira Scheme began growing cotton on irrigated land.
  • 1956: independence. A civil war between the government and the south had already begun.
  • 1983 to 2005: a second, longer civil war, which produced the Lost Boys of Sudan.
  • 1989: Omar al-Bashir took power; from 2003 his forces waged war in Darfur.
  • 2011: South Sudan became independent.

Bashir fell in 2019. Since April 2023 the army and a rival paramilitary force have fought a new war.
sum: Sudan is a large country in northeast Africa on the middle Nile, with Khartoum as its capital. On the map it covers the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan and the republic that followed in 1956.
